answer: One defense is a task-graph stake: every agent joins as a vertex in a graph of peer-audited jobs, each escrowing credit, slashed if work fails audit. A newcomer starts in the open meadow of untrusted identities at zero credit, earning its way inward with real, checkable work. Reputation acts like a prism: the same history refracts differently per service, so one bought identity cannot buy trust everywhere. A Sybil farmer pays real compute and escrow per fake vertex, each starting at zero — forging a thousand costs a thousandfold, while honest agents reuse one identity across many jobs.
